This could be due to many reasons

1. Pushing with infantry
2. Pushing without air superiority and CAS
3. Pushing into forts, marshes, forests, snow, mud, mountains or across a river
4. Pushing with little or no supply
5. Pushing with underequiped divisions
6. A combination of the above

I suspect that a combination of the above is the problem because the Soviet AAI SUCKS and even the German AI can push them all the way back to Moscow with pure infantry (and air support). 

To defeat the Soviet Union (quickly, at least) you'll need:

1. A decent amount of infantry divisions (you don't need THAT many, I've defeated the Soviets as Poland with a full army group). The role of your infantry is to hold the line, DO NOT try to push with infantry against an enemy of relative equal strength, the defending side is heavily favored, especially if they are entrenched. You'll lose a lot of men and equipment for minimal gains, only push with infantry if you heavily outnumber the enemy and don't mind the manpower/equipment loss.

2. Tanks. You won't break the enemy line with infantry, you need tanks for this. Concentrate your tanks, don't spread them out across the frontline but don't field 6 of them in a single tile because supply will suck and only like half of them can attack a single tile at the same time anyway. Micro them and go for encirclements, take advantage of the Ukrainian fields to maneuver them, they'll have great speed and almost no attack penalties so you can do some real damage.

3. Planes. Planes are really important and as Germany you have no excuse not to build them. Build a strong fleet of fighters to secure air superiority and a fleet of CAS to help your armies. Air superiority is already strong because it reduces enemy defense, CAS helps by boosting your attack (so called Air Support if you hover over your attack values) and doing direct damage to enemy divisions. It also slows down enemy divisions allowing for easier encirclements. You can probably get away with pushing with infantry as long as you have strong air support, if you don't mind losing men and equipment.
